These kinds of dilemmas are actually inspired by something called the Asian Disease Problem, which was created by psychologists Amos Tversky as well as Daniel Kahneman back in the 1980s. Their research showed the way a problem is framed. It can completely change people's decisions, whether it's focused on gains, like “lives saved,” or losses, like “lives lost.” Even if all of the options are logically the same, we tend to make different of the choices just based on the way how the situation is worded.
